- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.75) and recent prices are rising — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.5) and recent prices are volatile — model lags or underreacts.
- When sentiment spikes to 1.0, model often overreacts and forecasts higher than true outcome — apply downward correction by 5–10%.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model tends to overpredict next period — reduce forecast by 2–5% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is consolidating, model often forecasts a false breakout — cap forecast at recent 10-day moving average.
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to overestimate late-period prices — apply a 3–5% downward adjustment for days 25–30 if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment is negative (0.0–0.3) and price is falling, model often underestimates the drop — adjust forecast downward by 3–7% to reflect sentiment-driven volatility.
